chunks: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'and a spirit from Him' (4:171). He said: It is the spirit of God — a created being. God created it in Adam and in Jesus.

key_terms.رُوحُ اللَّهِ: The spirit of God — the Imam clarifies this is a created being, not part of the divine essence
key_terms.مَخْلُوقَةٌ: Created being — key theological term asserting the spirit's createdness, opposing the idea of divine co-eternality
key_terms.وَرُوحٌ مِنْهُ: Quranic phrase from 4:171 regarding Jesus, interpreted here as denoting a created spirit bestowed by God

ai.seo_question: What does 'a spirit from Him' (4:171) mean in Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: Humran ibn A'yan, a companion of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), asked about the Quranic phrase 'a spirit from Him' (4:171) which describes Jesus. The Imam clarified that this spirit (ruh) is a created entity, not an uncreated divine essence, thus refuting any theological inference that Jesus shares in the divine nature. God created this spirit and placed it in both Adam and Jesus — both prophets receiving the same divinely created spirit.
